English 日本語 简体中文 Português 

 

 Project Maya 

 GLM-5.3 (744 B), GLM-5.3-Flash (321 B), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 (748 B), MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (428 B), Hy4-Flash (220 B) and Inkling 2 Mini (26 B) on your own GPU 
private and fast · one NVIDIA GPU or up to 16 · AMD and Windows · chat, pictures, OpenAI- and
Anthropic-compatible API · several requests at once 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Created and led by Peasant Smith ( @mw00 ), co-maintained
with @needmorevram 

 
 
 Project Maya is free. If it runs well on your PC, sponsoring it pays for the test hardware and the work on it. 

Models this size usually need a datacenter. Maya runs five of them on the hardware you already have:
 GLM-5.3 , GLM-5.3-Flash , DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 , MiniMax-M3.1-Flash and Hy4-Flash - and the smaller Inkling 2 Mini . Each model has an engine built for it. It
keeps the experts your conversation uses most on the GPU, the next ones in RAM and the rest on your NVMe SSD, and moves
them as you chat. It measures your GPUs, CPU, RAM and SSD and tunes itself to them. Nothing leaves your machine.

- Fast: up to 149 tokens/s on two RTX 5090s and an RTX 4090, 124 on two H100s, 118 on four RTX 4090s, 81 on one
 RTX PRO 6000, 30+ on a single RTX 5090. Real numbers from real users.
- Close to the original: Maya's own quants of GLM-5.3-Flash keep 97.7-99.2% of the FP8 model's zero-shot
 accuracy; DeepSeek V4.1 · Maya-S picks the same next token as the original 92.6% of the time, MiniMax M3.1 · Maya-S
 87.6% (the average over its categories).
- Plugs into your tools: OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API with tool calls, ready for coding agents.
- Several requests at once: up to 8 answered together with GLM-5.3-Flash, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and
 MiniMax-M3.1-Flash - for agents that run several sessions, or several people on one PC.
- Everything in the box: a chat and a live monitor in the browser, pictures on the models that read them, thinking
 levels, a Models page that downloads, loads and deletes models, a Turbo button, a one-command setup.

 Quick start

 

The setup asks which model you want, downloads it, builds everything once and starts the model . Then open
 Windows: START-MAYA.bat instead of ./setup.sh . More in Install.

All documentation: docs/README.md

 Pick your model

Every Maya quant is named after its model, then its tier - XS, S, M or L, by how many bits its experts keep. The setup
recommends one for your PC; to pick one yourself, give its setup id: ./setup.sh --model glm-maya-s24 .

 Model Maya quant · setup id Size Made for 
 --- --- ---: --- 
 GLM-5.3-Flash zai-org · MIT · 321 B, 18 B active · up to 1M context Maya-S (default) · glm-maya-s 96.5 GB PCs with a smaller memory pool (RAM and VRAM together) 
 Maya-S24 · glm-maya-s24 94.7 GB cards of 24 GB or less: 1.5 GB more of the card for experts, decode +14% 
 Maya-XS · glm-maya-xs 73.4 GB PCs with 64 GB of RAM and a 24 GB card, at 128K context 
 Maya-M · glm-maya-m 116 GB a bigger memory pool; calibrated toward tool calls and front-end code 
 Maya-M-Derisked · glm-maya-m-derisked 116 GB Maya-M with a weight edit by Blackfrost AI that reduces blanket refusals; experimental 
 Maya-L · glm-maya-l 156.3 GB the biggest memory pools; the closest to the original 
 GLM-5.3 zai-org · its own license · 744 B, 40 B active · up to 1M context · text only Maya-XS · glm-5.3-maya-xs 170.0 GB the whole model in a 192 GB memory pool (VRAM and RAM together); NVIDIA from the V100 on and AMD (details) 
 UD-IQ2 M (unsloth) · GLM-5.3-UD-IQ2 M 238.6 GB the biggest memory pools; closer to the original 
 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 DeepSeek · MIT · 748 B Maya-S (default) · deepseek-maya-s 340 GB any amount of memory: what VRAM and RAM don't hold is read from the SSD 
 Maya-XS (v2) · deepseek-maya-xs 277 GB the whole model in a 128 GB PC's memory (the Engram tables stay on the SSD); v2 is about 12% closer to the original and about 20% faster at writing than v1 - running the setup again offers the update 
 MiniMax-M3.1-Flash MiniMax · MiniMax Community License · 428 B, 23 B active · up to 1M context Maya-XS · minimax-maya-xs 93 GB the whole model in a 128 GB PC's memory 
 Maya-S · minimax-maya-s 122 GB closer to the original 
 Hy4-Flash Tencent · Tencent Hy License · 220 B · up to 1M context · reads pictures · NVIDIA, AMD on Linux Maya-XS · hy4-flash-maya-xs Maya-S · hy4-flash-maya-s Maya-M · hy4-flash-maya-m Maya-L · hy4-flash-maya-l 44.8 GB 53.0 GB 68.4 GB 89.5 GB each + one 63.4 GB n-gram table PCs with about 56-64 GB (Maya-XS; cards from 8 GB), 68-80 GB (Maya-S), 80-96 GB (Maya-M) or 104-128 GB (Maya-L) of RAM + VRAM; Maya-S, Maya-M and Maya-L on cards from 12 GB; the n-gram table stays on the SSD 
 Inkling 2 Mini Thinking Machines · Apache 2.0 · 26 B · up to 1M context · reads pictures · NVIDIA, AMD on Linux unsloth's UD-Q4 K XL GGUF · inkling-2-mini 17.6 GB cards from 8 GB: the experts that don't fit stay in RAM; the whole model in VRAM from 24 GB 

 Which model fits your PC? See docs/MEMORY.md for each model's recommended memory (VRAM + RAM together).

All of them run on NVIDIA from the V100 / RTX 20 on, and on AMD and Windows (see
What you need); Hy4-Flash runs on NVIDIA (Linux and Windows) and on AMD on Linux (Strix Halo / Gorgon Halo, Radeon cards) and reads pictures on every card that runs it (8 GB cards included). DeepSeek's sizes include its Engram tables. The setup also offers unsloth's GGUF and
turboderp's and LibertAIDAI's EXL3 quants of DeepSeek, orcarouter's abliterated DeepSeek, Mia-AiLab's EXL3 quant of MiniMax,
turboderp's EXL3 quants of GLM, Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next (CYBER-FROST) as its Q5 K M GGUF and Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next
itself as unsloth's UD-IQ2 XS GGUF, both with pictures
(its settings), and Tencent's own Q4 K M of Hy4-flash (AngelSlim's GGUF)
with MTP drafting (run on NVIDIA RTX 30 / A100 and newer, Linux; with pictures: ./maya.sh --setup --model hy4-flash-q4 k m ;
its settings), and Inkling 2 Mini (26 B) on its own engine:

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
git clone https://github.com/mw00/project-maya.git && cd project-maya
./setup.sh

The setup asks which model you want, downloads it, builds everything once and starts the model. Then open http://127.0.0.1:8080. Windows: START-MAYA.bat instead of ./setup.sh. More in Install.

All documentation: docs/README.md

usage.title: Using it
usage.html:
• In the browser: chat (kept in your browser, with search, pins and folders, per-chat instructions and thinking level, edit and regenerate, HTML previews), a live Monitor of the model and your hardware (down to what fills each GPU's memory), a context size and port you can change in Settings, and Models: every model set up on this machine, switching to another (Maya starts again with it) and each one's engine settings (context, GPUs, drafting, images, memory), saved into its maya-<model>.json.
  • Models page: the catalog lists every Maya model with its size. Download one with a progress bar, load it, unload the running one or delete one - no command line needed.
  • Turbo: one button beside the model's parameters sets the fastest settings for the model (greedy sampling, no thinking, expert skipping, the fastest drafting). It trades some quality for speed; switching it off restores your settings exactly.
  • Saved: the sidebar's Saved line adds up what the model's own API (DeepSeek's, Z.ai's, MiniMax's or Tencent's) would have charged for the same tokens - the prompt Maya reuses from its cache at the API's cached price, DeepSeek's peak hours at its peak price - kept per model in token-savings.json; its prices can be changed in Settings › Savings.
  • Your apps and coding agents: an OpenAI-compatible API at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1, and Anthropic's at http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/messages (Claude Code: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080). Tool calls are streamed as the model writes them, and a long prompt's reading progress too when a request asks for it ("return_progress": true). A web page served from another address can call it too once you allow its address ("cors_origins", docs/SETUP.md).
  • Responses API: /v1/responses supports text/image conversations, streaming, function tool calls, schema-validated output, background tasks with cancellation/replay, and optional shared in-memory history (store:true, previous_response_id). Responses are not stored by default. Options and limits: docs/RESPONSES.md.
  • Model API: /api/tags, /api/ps, /api/show, /api/chat, /api/generate, /api/pull and /api/delete list, load, download and delete models from any app or script. A request for a model that is not loaded swaps to it, and keep_alive unloads it when idle. /models/load, /models/unload and /models/sse are on by default too ("model_management": false turns them off).
  • Thinking: Off, Low, High (the default) or Max, in Settings or per request, and a thinking budget field that sets how many tokens the model may think before it answers.
  • Loop guard: on by default - an agent that repeats the same tool call with the same result is steered off it.
  • Pictures: attach one in the chat, or send image parts through either API. Every model reads them except GLM-5.3, which is text only - and Hy4-Flash on 8 GB cards (setup details per model: docs/MODELS.md). Videos too, for the models that read them.
  • Files: attach any file in the chat. Text and code go in as they are; PDFs as their text, or a scanned one's first pages as pictures; Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OpenDocument, EPUB and RTF files as their text. Anything Maya can't read says why. The same works through the APIs: OpenAI file / input_file parts and Anthropic document blocks (sent inline). poppler, when installed (sudo apt install poppler-utils), reads PDFs a little better; it is optional.
  • MCP tools: list MCP servers in the config ("mcp_servers"; Claude Desktop's mcpServers block works as it is) and the web chat's model can call their tools. A switch in the chat's + menu turns them on and off. What it does: serve/mcp.py.
  • Docker: there is no official image. docs/DOCKER.md is a recipe to build one from a release.
  • From another device: ./maya.sh --setup --host 0.0.0.0 --api-key <secret>. Always set a key.
  • Tuning: ./maya.sh --calibrate tunes the engine to your hardware in 10-15 minutes. Every setting: docs/SETTINGS.md.
  • Each model's own options - GLM-5.3-Flash's several requests at once (--parallel), long contexts and DFlash2 drafter; DeepSeek's kept conversations, expert loading and Engram read-ahead; MiniMax's thinking levels: docs/MODELS.md.
